note: Longest recorded length of each species from a named source (the largest such, so that no real fish is ruled out; compilations without an attributed source are left out), converted between TL and SL with FishBase's length-length relationship for the species (TL = b x SL; the mean where it lists several; the median of the others where it lists none). Names: the accepted name, every synonym GBIF's backbone lists, FishBase's valid name, and names museum labels carry from Gilbert 1964, Scott & Crossman 1973 and FishBase. Collected 2026-10-25.

species.name: Luxilus cornutus
species.max_source: Scott & Crossman 1973, Freshwater Fishes of Canada, Bull. Fish. Res. Board Can. 184, p. 451: largest known, a male from Lake Bernard, Que.
species.tl_per_sl_source: FishBase length-length: TL = 1.159 SL and 1.192 SL
other_maxima: 180 mm TL, Page & Burr 2011, 2nd ed. (FishBase Ref. 86798)
ca. 175 mm, length not stated, Gilbert 1964, Bull. Florida State Mus. 8(2), Table 3
species.notes: The largest fish are breeding males. Until Gilbert (1961, 1964) the striped shiner was Notropis cornutus chrysocephalus, so a pre-1964 lot labelled Notropis cornutus from the Ohio or Mississippi basin may be L. chrysocephalus.

species.name: Luxilus chrysocephalus
species.max_source: Etnier & Starnes 1993, The Fishes of Tennessee, p. 183: 'Maximum total length 240 mm (9.3 in) reported by Marshall (1939)'
other_maxima: ca. 175 mm, length not stated, Gilbert 1964, Table 3
163 mm SL figured breeding male, Etnier & Starnes 1993, The Fishes of Tennessee, plate 53b
species.notes: The 240 mm rests on one report (Marshall 1939); treat it as a ceiling.

species.name: Notropis atherinoides
species.max_source: Etnier & Starnes 1993, The Fishes of Tennessee, p. 212, from Trautman 1957 (Ohio)
other_maxima: 130 mm TL, Page & Burr 1991, A Field Guide to Freshwater Fishes of North America North of Mexico (FishBase Ref. 5723)
103 mm TL, largest in ROM collections, Scott & Crossman 1973, Freshwater Fishes of Canada, Bull. Fish. Res. Board Can. 184, p. 442
99 mm TL, largest Etnier & Starnes saw
species.notes: Regional sizes differ widely; 132 mm (Lake Erie region) is well above most collections.

species.name: Notropis rubellus
species.max_source: Parker, Fritts & DeBoer 2018, J. Appl. Ichthyol. 34:1081-1083 (FishBase Ref. 121533)
other_maxima: 90 mm TL, Page & Burr 1991, A Field Guide to Freshwater Fishes of North America North of Mexico (FishBase Ref. 5723)
99 mm TL, Central Appalachia, FishBase max. ages/sizes
75 mm SL, largest female in Pfeiffer's 1955 sample, Scott & Crossman 1973, Freshwater Fishes of Canada, Bull. Fish. Res. Board Can. 184, p. 465
76 mm TL, Tennessee form, Etnier & Starnes 1993, The Fishes of Tennessee, p. 221
species.notes: The 110 mm is from a Midwestern sample that may include N. percobromus (split from rubellus in 2002). Kept as the ceiling so a large true rubellus is not ruled out; rubellus sensu stricto records run 90-99 mm TL.

species.name: Hudsonius hudsonius
species.max_source: Page & Burr 1991, A Field Guide to Freshwater Fishes of North America North of Mexico (FishBase Ref. 5723)
other_maxima: 132 mm TL, largest in ROM collections (Lake Erie), Scott & Crossman 1973, Freshwater Fishes of Canada, Bull. Fish. Res. Board Can. 184, p. 462
species.notes: Lake Erie fish run large; spottails over 127 mm TL are unusual elsewhere (Scott & Crossman).

species.name: Paranotropis volucellus
species.max_source: Page & Burr 1991, A Field Guide to Freshwater Fishes of North America North of Mexico (FishBase Ref. 5723)
other_maxima: 65 mm TL, Tennessee forms, Etnier & Starnes 1993, The Fishes of Tennessee, p. 232
species.notes: Moved to Paranotropis by Stout et al. 2022 (PeerJ 10:e14072) and Page et al. 2023. A complex: older lots labelled N. volucellus wickliffi or N. v. buchanani may be P. wickliffi or P. buchanani, now species of their own.

species.name: Notropis bifrenatus
species.max_source: COSEWIC 2013, status report on the Bridle Shiner, citing Holm, Mandrak & Burridge 2010, ROM Field Guide to Freshwater Fishes of Ontario
